subject: Request: Threat model walkthrough and network diagram for inference zones

From: Elena Navarro <elena.navarro@argenta.com>

Cc: security@argenta.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Threat model walkthrough and network diagram for inference zones

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the demo last week. Argenta's security team is compiling a technical dossier for our vendor risk board and we've scoped Redwood as a shortlisted inference provider. To complete our review we need the following technical artifacts and a short walkthrough:

- A current network/topology diagram that highlights tenant boundaries, egress control points, and control plane endpoints.
- A written summary (1-2 pages) of the isolation model you use between tenants and between control plane and data plane.
- Threat model summary focused on lateral movement, KV-cache leakage, and cross-tenant inference data exfiltration (including mitigations).
- Evidence/examples of egress filter enforcement and audit logs for a representative edge region.

Our timeline is tight — can you provide a draft by EOD Friday (18 Jun)? If that's not feasible, please propose an alternate delivery date.

Also, can you indicate any parts of the diagram that will be redacted for IP reasons? We understand diagrams may be high-level.

Thanks,
Elena Navarro
Senior Vendor Risk Manager
Argenta Financial Technologies
elena.navarro@argenta.com
+1 415-555-2197

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask and for including the target scope. We can deliver a concise package that covers the diagram, isolation summary, and threat model write-up by EOD Friday.

Plan:
- Deliverable v1 (by 2026-06-18 EOD): redacted topology diagram, 2-page isolation summary, 1-page threat model highlights, and an evidence index (what we can provide directly vs. what requires an NDA/controlled access).
- Follow-up (week of 2026-06-21): an optional 30–45 minute technical walkthrough with our infra/security leads.

Monica — looping you and Karthik in to draft the documents and collect the evidence stubs (audit log examples, egress ACL screenshots). Vanessa, FYI on the canary/egress discussion since Argenta asked for region-specific enforcement examples.

We will redact internal IPs and exact operator network prefixes; diagrams will show functional components and control/data plane boundaries. If Argenta needs more granular evidence we can arrange a signed NDA and screen-share for live logs.

Sean Gallagher

Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft packet for Argenta — please review

Team — initial draft attached (links below) and some inline notes. Please review, edit, and forward any additional evidence items by EOD Thu so I can package the v1 deliverable on Friday.

Attachments (drafts/stubs):
- redwood_inference_zone_diagram_v2.svg (redacted operator IPs; shows tenant enclave, sidecar boundary, control plane endpoint, egress proxy)
- kv-cache-isolation-matrix.xlsx (matrix of KV cache lifecycle, per-tenant namespace, retention and access controls)
- egress_control_evidence_summary.pdf (contains screenshots from staging region: ACL rules, bastion access logs, and sample audit entries)

Inline notes:
1) Diagram: I flagged the dashed arrow for cross-region fallbacks — ensure language clarifies that cached artifacts never cross tenant boundaries and that cross-region routing is on a model-variant fallback path only (no shared KV between tenants).
2) Threat model: Karthik, please add a short note on mitigations for sidecar compromise and replay attacks (token scoping, short-lived session keys, and cache key namespacing).
3) Evidence: Monica, can you pull one redacted audit trace for an egress ACL enforcement event from us-west-2 (timestamped) and a sample control-plane auth log? Include the minimal fields needed for verification.

Suggested edits to the isolation summary: avoid operational runbook details that reveal handshake secrets — we should keep it architecture + controls. If Argenta requests more, request an NDA and then share logs via the secure folder.

Thanks —
Sean
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2026 11:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft packet for Argenta — please review

SEAN / MONICA — quick inputs below; pasted for the packet.

- Sidecar compromise: we implement mandatory per-tenant mTLS + short-lived mTLS identities issued by the control plane (10–15 minute TTL). The sidecar process can only access the KV cache through a namespace enforced by the runtime; namespaces are cryptographically keyed. Add a sentence: "Even in a sidecar runtime compromise, cryptographic separation of KV namespaces prevents access to other tenants' cached state."

- KV cache lifecycle: current policy is TTL-based eviction with additional explicit namespace wipe on model swap or tenant offboarding; matrix spreadsheet updated in column F with TTL defaults and offboarding procedure reference (internal runbook id: OPS-KV-23).

- Lateral movement mitigations: policy-enforced host microsegmentation, continuous workload attestation (runtime checks), and automated circuit breakers that quarantine noisy instances. Recommend we include a short example: "If anomalous token usage is observed, the instance circuit-breaker toggles to deny new sessions and triggers an operator workflow."

Attachments to include in final: updated SVG, updated XLSX, and a redacted log snippet (Monica to add). I avoided operational playbook text.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
